Międzyrzec Podlaski Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Międzyrzec Podlaski, Poland

Demolished. Międzyrzec Podlaski's Jewish community, documented from at least 1533, grew to an extraordinary 84 percent of the town's roughly 18,000 residents by the late interwar period. From the 18th century, local Jews specialized in brush-making. This, the town's old cemetery, is first referenced in 1605 and was used until 1810, when a new cemetery opened; it was destroyed at the end of 1939, when Germans established a forced-labor selection site there, and the area was later mined for clay and sand before being built over in 1946. In 1946, 30 matzevot recovered from the town and surrounding area, dated 1709 to 1809, were embedded in the wall of the new cemetery, documented elsewhere in this collection.
